title: Anthropic's Mythos and the macOS Exploit
caption:
Anthropic's Mythos, a research AI, just helped researchers crack macOS security. It's a stark reminder: AI's dual-use nature means it can find exploits as easily as it can fix them. The implications for cybersecurity are massive.

* AI is changing the attack surface for operating systems.

Tap BUILD to get the field guide on AI security.

slides.headline: Anthropic’s AI Just *Cracked* macOS Security.
slides.sub: A research model exposed critical privacy flaws.

slides.definition: Anthropic's internal research model, a less publicized sibling to Claude. It's designed for advanced R&D, exploring new frontiers in AI capabilities and safety.
slides.example: Researchers leveraged Mythos to probe system vulnerabilities.

slides.title: How Mythos Found The Flaw
slides.body: Security researchers tasked Mythos with identifying weaknesses in macOS privacy settings. The AI successfully pinpointed a critical vulnerability that could bypass user consent for data access.

slides.title: What Was Exposed
bullets: A flaw in macOS privacy settings.
Allowed applications to access sensitive user data without explicit permission.
slides.footer: This wasn't a zero-day but a proof-of-concept for AI-assisted vulnerability discovery.

audiences.body: AI can rapidly identify complex system vulnerabilities, accelerating exploit development for malicious actors.
AI can also be a powerful tool for proactively finding and patching security gaps before they are exploited.

slides.quote: Our goal is to understand the full spectrum of AI capabilities, including potential misuse, to build safer systems. This research helps us do that.

slides.hook: The future of cybersecurity will be *AI-driven*.
slides.sub: Understand the tools shaping tomorrow's digital battleground.
